claims.text: Pods are the smallest deployable units of computing that you can create and manage in Kubernetes; a Pod is a group of one or more containers whose contents are always co-located and co-scheduled on the same node.
Kubernetes places (schedules) Pods, not individual containers, onto nodes; all containers of a Pod run on the Pod's node and are removed with the Pod.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Pods (Pods and controllers, Pod lifecycle)

claims.text: Each Pod is assigned a unique IP (hostNetwork system Pods in kube-system use their node's IP instead); containers in a Pod share the network namespace, IP and ports, and communicate using localhost.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Pods (Pod networking); Cluster Networking

claims.text: Containers in one Pod share one port space and must coordinate port use; whether a second listener on the same port fails depends on the program (two caddy containers can both bind :80 via port reuse).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pods (Pod networking: containers must coordinate how they use shared network resources such as ports)

claims.text: Most Pods run a single container ('one-container-per-Pod' is the most common use case); multiple containers in one Pod are for tightly coupled helpers that need to share resources such as network or volumes.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Pods (Using Pods; Pods that run multiple containers)

claims.text: Opinion: an app and its database should not share a Pod, because containers in one Pod start, stop, scale and are replaced together; a second copy of the Pod would bring its own database.
claims.source_hint: outline item 4; kubernetes.io Pods (Pods are designed as relatively ephemeral; scaling replicates the whole Pod)

claims.text: docker-compose.yml@stage-2: web uses network_mode "service:lab" (shares the lab service's network stack and address); db and api have own addresses on the donhang network (172.28.0.11, 172.28.0.13).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 docker-compose.yml web service (line 48); lesson devops.l1.docker-networks

claims.text: deploy/k8s/lessons/web-pod.yaml@stage-2: apiVersion v1, kind Pod, metadata.name web, one container named web with image caddy:2.10.0 and containerPort 80; no namespace field.
With the image's default configuration, caddy:2.10.0 serves Caddy's built-in welcome page on port 80.
claims.source_hint: Docker Hub caddy image docs (default Caddyfile serves welcome page on :80); web-pod.yaml comment lines 3-4

claims.text: containerPort in a container spec is primarily informational: it lists a port the container exposes; not specifying it does not prevent the port from being reachable.
claims.source_hint: kubectl explain pod.spec.containers.ports; Pod API reference (ports)

claims.text: A Pod's IP is assigned when the Pod is set up, from the cluster's Pod address range (kind 10.244.0.0/16); in the donhang kind cluster it is not reachable from the laptop; a replacement Pod should not be expected to keep the IP.
claims.source_hint: kubectl explain pod.status.podIP ('Routable at least within the cluster'); Cluster Networking; Service concept (Pods are ephemeral, IPs change)

claims.text: kubectl explain pod.spec.containers prints FIELD: containers <[]Container> and 'There must be at least one container in a Pod'; kubectl explain pod.status.podIP prints 'podIP address allocated to the pod'. kubectl explain reads the API schema and creates nothing.
claims.source_hint: executed kubectl v1.34.3 against kind v1.34.11; kubectl explain reference

claims.text: Containers in one Pod can share files through a volume mounted into each of them; a Pod is replaced as a whole, and running more copies means more Pods, each with all its containers.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pods (Resource sharing and communication: Storage in Pods; Pods and controllers, replication)

claims.text: The container spec (kubectl explain pod.spec.containers) has no IP address field; the only Pod address field is status.podIP (plus podIPs).
claims.source_hint: executed kubectl explain pod.spec.containers / pod.status; Pod API reference
